description: Curated library of authentic Stoic quotes for content generation. Each quote includes the original source, thematic tags for matching, and the exact wording.

Marcus Aurelius.text: You have power over your mind — not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
The best revenge is to be unlike him who performed the injury.
When you arise in the morning, think of what a privilege it is to be alive — to breathe, to think, to enjoy, to love.
Very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
The soul becomes dyed with the color of its thoughts.
It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live.
Dwell on the beauty of life. Watch the stars, and see yourself running with them.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
Look within. Within is the fountain of good, and it will ever bubble up, if you will ever dig.
Everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact. Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.
Loss is nothing else but change, and change is Nature's delight.
Nowhere you can go is more peaceful — more free of interruptions — than your own soul.
What is not good for the hive is not good for the bee.
The universe is change; our life is what our thoughts make it.
Accept whatever comes to you woven in the pattern of your destiny, for what could more aptly fit your needs?
Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life.
Never let the future disturb you. You will meet it, if you have to, with the same weapons of reason which arm you against the present.
To live a good life: We have the potential for it. If we can learn to be indifferent to what makes no difference.
The art of living is more like wrestling than dancing.
What we do now echoes in eternity.
Each day, tell yourself: today I shall meet people who are meddling, ungrateful, arrogant — but I, against my will, have been wronged by none.
You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do and say and think.
If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
The first rule is to keep an untroubled spirit. The second is to look things in the face and know them for what they are.
Receive without pride, let go without attachment.
How much more grievous are the consequences of anger than the causes of it.
You always own the option of having no opinion. There is never any need to get worked up.
Everything that happens, happens as it should, and if you observe carefully, you will find this to be true.

Seneca.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
Sometimes even to live is an act of courage.
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
He who is brave is free.
Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for kindness.
True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future.
Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
We should every night call ourselves to account: What weakness have I overcome today?
A man's life is dyed by his imagination.
It's not because things are difficult that we dare not; it's because we dare not that they are difficult.
Hang on to your youthful enthusiasms — you'll be able to use them better when you're older.
Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.
Most powerful is he who has himself in his own power.
If a man knows not to which port he sails, no wind is favorable.
It is quality rather than quantity that matters.
No man was ever wise by chance.
Associate with people who are likely to improve you.
While we wait for life, life passes.
The whole future lies in uncertainty: live immediately.
To be everywhere is to be nowhere.
What fortune has made yours is not your own.
A sword never kills anyone; it is a tool in the killer's hand.
Anger, if not restrained, is frequently more hurtful to us than the injury that provokes it.
The greatest wealth is a poverty of desires.
We should take wandering outdoor walks, so that the mind might be refreshed and invigorated.
What need is there to weep over parts of life? The whole of it calls for tears.
It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
Do not ask for what you will get if you ask for what you do not need.
It is a rough road that leads to the heights of greatness.
Fire tests gold, suffering tests brave men.
We are more often frightened than hurt; and we suffer more from imagination than from reality.
Life is long if you know how to use it.
Let all your efforts be directed to something, let it keep that end in view.

Epictetus.text: People are not disturbed by things, but by the views they take of them.
First say to yourself what you would be; then do what you have to do.
Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.
No great thing is created suddenly.
Freedom is the only worthy goal in life. It is won by disregarding things that lie beyond our control.
He is a wise man who does not grieve for the things which he has not, but rejoices for those which he has.
Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
It's not what happens to you, but how you react to it that matters.
Any person capable of angering you becomes your master.
The key is to keep company only with people who uplift you, whose presence calls forth your best.
If you want to improve, be content to be thought foolish and stupid.
Circumstances do not rise to meet our expectations. Events happen as they do. People behave as they are. Embrace what you actually get.
There is only one way to happiness — cease worrying about things which are beyond the power of our will.
Don't explain your philosophy. Embody it.
First learn the meaning of what you say, and then speak.
What would have become of Hercules if there had been no lion, no hydra, no boar? He would have remained unknown.
We cannot choose our external circumstances, but we can always choose how we respond to them.
The greater the difficulty, the more glory in surmounting it.
It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.
If you wish to be a writer, write. If you wish to be a good person, be good. It begins with action, not intention.
You are a little soul carrying around a corpse.
Silliness and ignorance create all difficulties.
Don't be concerned with what others think. There is no higher rule than your own integrity.
Seek not that the things which happen should happen as you wish; but wish the things which happen to be as they are, and you will have a tranquil flow of life.
Nature has given man one tongue but two ears, that we may hear more than we speak.
You are not your body. You are not your thoughts. You are the observer of both.
Who is your master? Anyone who has power over things you desire or avoid.
The essence of philosophy is that a man should live so that his happiness depends as little as possible on external things.
When you close your doors and make darkness within, remember never to say that you are alone. You are not alone; God is within.
Practice yourself, for heaven's sake, in little things; and from them proceed to greater.

Zeno.text: Man conquers the world by conquering himself.
Wellbeing is attained by little and little, and nevertheless is no little thing itself.
We have two ears and one mouth, so we should listen more than we say.
The end of life is to live in agreement with nature.
Nothing is more hostile to a firm grasp of knowledge than self-deception.
Better to trip with the feet than with the tongue.
The reason we have two ears and only one mouth is that we may hear more and speak less.
All things are parts of one single system, which is called Nature.
Virtue is the only good. Everything else is indifferent.
Happiness is a good flow of life.
When a dog is tied to a cart, if it wants to follow, it is pulled and follows, making its act coincide with necessity. But if it does not want to follow, it will be compelled in any case.
Steer your course with virtue, for it alone can guide you through the storm.
The foundation of every state is the education of its youth.
A bad feeling is a commotion of the mind repugnant to reason, and against nature.
The most important lesson is that we are all part of a greater whole.
Fate guides the willing, but drags the unwilling.
Live your life with virtue as your guide, for all else is secondary.
The goal of life is to live in harmony with nature, which means living virtuously.
A friend is another self.
Happiness requires not possessions but virtues.
The whole world is our country, and all people are our fellow citizens.
Let us learn to live with what is within our power, and be indifferent to what is not.
Worthwhile things take time. Do not expect to harvest what you have not planted.
A small flame can light a great fire. Begin where you are.
The wise person lives in harmony with all that exists, understanding the interconnectedness of all things.
No one entrusts a secret to a drunken man; but one entrusts a secret to a good man. So goodness is stronger than wine.

Musonius Rufus.text: If you pursue the good, you will become good. If you pursue the bad, you will become bad.
We should train ourselves not to be easily upset by the misfortunes that happen to us.
The goal of life is to live in accordance with nature, which means living virtuously.
Virtue is the only true good, and vice the only true evil.
One who is not educated in philosophy is not truly free.
What use is knowledge if it does not lead to right action?
We should learn to bear pain with courage, to endure hardship with patience, and to face death with dignity.
The person who is kind and generous to all living things is in harmony with nature.
A human being's highest purpose is to serve others with wisdom and justice.
Let us not strive to be rich, but to be good. For goodness brings true wealth.
Practice is more important than theory. For what good is knowing what to do if you do not do it?
We should be as ready to listen as we are to speak, for wisdom comes from understanding, not from talking.
One who has learned to bear misfortune bravely has overcome a great evil.
To live virtuously is to live in harmony with nature, and this is the only path to genuine happiness.
If you accomplish something good with hard work, the labor passes quickly, but the good endures.
It is disgraceful for a person to grow old without ever seeing the beauty and strength of which their soul is capable.
We ought to remember that we are human beings, born to help one another.
The good person is neither elated by prosperity nor cast down by adversity.
Pleasure is not the goal of life. Virtue is.
The philosopher is a physician of the soul, not a maker of fine speeches.
One who does not know how to listen does not know how to learn.
Courage is not the absence of fear, but the judgment that something is more important than fear.
We should not measure a person by their wealth, but by their character.
The person who is always learning is always growing, and the one who stops learning stops living.
Let us not simply learn virtue, but live it.
When you help another, you help yourself. For we are all connected.
Patience is the companion of wisdom. Without it, even the wise become fools.
A life without purpose is a life without meaning. Find your purpose and live it fully.
The measure of a person is not what they say, but what they do.
Let your deeds be your philosophy. For what you do speaks louder than what you claim to believe.
